text:
JJ Peterka is on his third team in three seasons, from Buffalo to Utah to Boston, and the fresh start is going well. He's playing 17:36 a night, up from just under 16 last season, with his ice time climbing to nearly 19 minutes over the last ten games. He has 14 points in 18 games.

The part that makes this a breakout rather than a hot streak is the chances. His expected goals per 60 minutes are up to 1.19 from 0.73, and his finishing is right on target (5 goals on 6.3 expected). Boston gets 55% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, three points better than without.

One caution: like most Bruins forwards, he's on the ice for more goals than the chances deserve (6.3 more), which helps the assist total. Evolving-Hockey's read on last season was that he was better than his results, around replacement level by goals but 1.5 wins by chance quality. This season the results are catching up. Watch the minutes: the coach keeps giving him more.
headline: Peterka's new start in Boston is working
